questions.question: Which of the following is an example of bulky organic manure?
questions.explanation: Bulky organic manures include FYM, compost, and green manure, which add organic matter and nutrients to the soil. Urea, ammonium sulphate, superphosphate, and potassium chloride are inorganic fertilizers, not manures.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following manures is prepared by decomposing cow dung, urine, and farm waste?
questions.explanation: FYM is made by decomposing cow dung, urine, and agricultural waste over time. Vermicompost is prepared using earthworms. Green manure is made by plowing leguminous crops back into the soil. Bone meal and oil cakes are by-products of the animal and oil industries.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following is a nitrogen-rich organic manure?
questions.explanation: Neem cake is an organic manure rich in nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium (NPK). Superphosphate and rock phosphate are phosphorus fertilizers, not organic manures. Bone meal provides phosphorus but is not rich in nitrogen. Gypsum is used to improve soil structure, not as a nitrogen source.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Green manure crops improve soil fertility mainly by
questions.explanation: Green manure crops, such as legumes, improve soil fertility in multiple ways - Adding organic matter when plowed into the soil. Fixing atmospheric nitrogen (e.g., Sesbania, Crotalaria). Enhancing soil structure and microbial diversity.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is the approximate nitrogen (N) content in Farm Yard Manure (FYM)?
questions.explanation: The nitrogen content in FYM is approximately 0.5%. It also contains 0.2% phosphorus (P2O5) and 0.5% potassium (K2O).[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is the main difference between FYM and cattle urine in terms of nutrient composition?

options.a: Cattle urine contains more phosphorus than FYM
options.b: FYM has more nitrogen than cattle urine
options.c: Cattle urine has higher nitrogen and potassium content than FYM
options.d: FYM has more potassium than cattle urine

questions.explanation: Cattle urine contains 1.0% nitrogen and 1.35% potassium, which is higher than the nitrogen (0.5%) and potassium (0.5%) content in FYM. However, FYM contains phosphorus (0.2%), while cattle urine has very little phosphorus.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is compost?

options.b: A mass of rotten organic matter made from organic waste

questions.explanation: Compost is decomposed organic matter made from plant residues, farm waste, and kitchen waste. It improves soil fertility by adding organic matter and nutrients.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following conditions is required for proper composting?
questions.explanation: Composting requires moisture, oxygen, and microbial activity for efficient decomposition. Anaerobic conditions slow down decomposition and cause bad odors.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is the approximate nitrogen (N) content in compost?
questions.explanation: Compost contains approximately 0.5% nitrogen (N), 0.15% phosphorus (P2O5), and 0.5% potassium (K2O).[cite: 5]

questions.question: Among the following, which nutrient is present in the lowest quantity in compost?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus content in compost is only 0.15%, which is lower compared to nitrogen (0.5%) and potassium (0.5%).[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about compost?

options.c: It has equal amounts of nitrogen and potassium

questions.explanation: Compost has 0.5% nitrogen (N) and 0.5% potassium (K2O), while phosphorus (P2O5) is lower (0.15%). It contains organic matter and enhances soil fertility.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is night soil?

options.c: A type of compost made from food waste

questions.explanation: Night soil refers to human excreta (both solid and liquid) used as organic manure. It is richer in nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium than farmyard manure (FYM) and compost.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which nutrient is present in the highest percentage in night soil?
questions.explanation: Night soil contains approximately 5.5% nitrogen (N), 0.4% phosphorus (P), and 2.0% potassium (K). Nitrogen is the most abundant nutrient in night soil, essential for vegetative growth in plants.[cite: 5]

questions.question: How does night soil compare to farmyard manure (FYM) in terms of nutrient content?

options.a: Night soil has lower nutrients than FYM
options.b: Night soil has higher nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium than FYM
options.c: FYM contains more nitrogen than night soil
options.d: Night soil is only used for acidic soils

questions.explanation: Night soil is richer in N (5.5%), P (0.4%), and K (2.0%) compared to farmyard manure, which has lower nutrient concentrations.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is vermicompost?

options.b: Compost prepared with the help of earthworms

questions.explanation: Vermicompost is a nutrient-rich organic fertilizer created using earthworms, which consume organic matter and excrete nutrient-rich castings.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is the approximate nitrogen (N) content in vermicompost?
questions.explanation: Vermicompost contains about 3% nitrogen (N), 1% phosphorus (P), and 1.5% potassium (K), making it a balanced organic fertilizer.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is the role of earthworm castings in vermicompost?

options.a: Contain plant nutrients and beneficial microbes

questions.explanation: Earthworm castings are rich in essential nutrients (NPK), enzymes, and beneficial microbes like bacteria and mycorrhizae, which enhance soil health and crop productivity.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following statements about vermicompost is TRUE?

options.a: Vermicompost is only a source of nitrogen and does not provide other nutrients.
options.b: It contains both major and minor plant nutrients, making it a balanced organic fertilizer.
options.c: It reduces the microbial population in the soil.
options.d: It provides a quick response to the crop but lacks minor nutrients.

questions.explanation: Vermicompost is a rich mixture of major and minor plants nutrients. It is an excellent base for establishment of beneficial free living and symbiotic microbes.[cite: 5]

questions.question: How does vermicompost contribute to soil microbial activity?

options.a: It inhibits the growth of beneficial bacteria.
options.b: It increases the population of nitrogen-fixing bacteria, actinomycetes, and VAM (vesicular arbuscular mycorrhiza).
options.c: It eliminates all microorganisms from the soil.

questions.explanation: Vermicompost is a rich mixture of major and minor plants nutrients. It is an excellent base for establishment of beneficial free living and symbiotic microbes. Vermicompost increase the nitrogen fixing bacteria, actinomycetes, and VAM (vesicular arbuscular mycorrhizal) population in soil.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following is an important green manure crop?
questions.explanation: Common green manure crops include sunhemp, dhaincha, pillipesara, cluster beans, and sesbania rostrata, which help in nitrogen fixation and soil enrichment.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What makes Sesbania rostrata unique among green manure crops?

options.a: It is native to South America
options.b: It forms stem nodules for nitrogen fixation
options.c: It does not contribute to nitrogen fixation

questions.explanation: Unlike other legumes, Sesbania rostrata can fix nitrogen through stem nodules in addition to root nodules, making it highly efficient for soil fertility improvement.[cite: 5]

questions.question: How can nitrogen fixation in green manure crops be increased?

options.d: By growing crops in dry, barren soil

questions.explanation: Phosphorus is essential for root development and helps enhance the nitrogen-fixing ability of leguminous crops by supporting rhizobia activity.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which green manure crop is most effective for improving sodic soils?
questions.explanation: Gliricidia is particularly effective in reclaiming sodic soils due to its deep-root system and ability to enhance organic matter.[cite: 5]

questions.question: How does green manure contribute to weed management?

options.b: By suppressing weed growth through dense canopy cover
options.c: By competing with weeds for nutrients
options.d: By occupying the soil space in the off-season

questions.explanation: Green manure crops suppress weed growth through competition, shading, and release of natural chemicals that inhibit weed germination.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following green manure crop contains the highest amount of nitrogen?
questions.explanation: Dhaincha contains - 3.50% of nitrogen. Compared to Sunhemp (1.30%), Sesibenia speciosa (2.71%), Gliricidia sepium (2.76%), and Neem (2.83%).[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following statements about sheep and goat manure is TRUE?

options.a: It has lower nutrient content than farmyard manure.
options.b: It contains higher nutrients than farmyard manure and compost.
options.c: It does not contribute to soil fertility.

questions.explanation: Sheep and goat manure is richer in nitrogen (3%), phosphorus (1%), and potassium (2%) compared to farmyard manure and compost.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is the nitrogen content of sheep and goat manure?
questions.explanation: Sheep and goat manure is particularly rich in nitrogen (3%), which promotes plant growth and soil fertility.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is Sheep Penning in soil fertility management?

options.a: A method of composting sheep manure.
options.b: Keeping sheep and goats overnight in the field to improve soil fertility through urine and faecal deposition.
options.c: A technique for reducing manure usage in farming.
options.d: A practice of confining sheep in a barn to collect manure.

questions.explanation: Sheep penning is an organic soil enrichment technique where sheep and goats are allowed to graze and rest overnight in the field, adding nutrients through their urine and droppings.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which bulky organic manure contains the highest amount of nitrogen and phosphorus?
questions.explanation: Poultry manure has the highest nitrogen (3.30%) and phosphorus (2.63%) content compared to other bulky manures.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What happens when poultry manure is left exposed for 30 days?

options.d: It becomes more effective as fertilizer.

questions.explanation: If poultry manure is left exposed, nitrogen is lost through volatilization, reducing its effectiveness as a fertilizer by 50%.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is the phosphorus (P2O5) content in poultry manure?
questions.explanation: Poultry manure contains approximately 2.63% phosphorus, making it one of the richest organic sources of phosphorus.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following manures has the highest nitrogen (N) content?
questions.explanation: Night soil contains the highest nitrogen content (5.5%) compared to other bulky manures.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which manure contains the highest phosphorus (P2O5) content?
questions.explanation: Poultry manure has the highest phosphorus content (2.63%), making it a rich source of this nutrient.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which manure has the most balanced composition of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium (NPK)?
questions.explanation: Compost contains nitrogen (1.4%), phosphorus (1.0%), and potassium (1.4%), making it a well-balanced manure.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which manure has the lowest nitrogen content among the listed options?
questions.explanation: Farmyard manure has the lowest nitrogen content (0.5%) compared to other bulky manures.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which manure is known to have the highest potassium (K2O) content?
questions.explanation: Sheep and goat manure contains the highest potassium content (2.0%), making it beneficial for potassium-deficient soils.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is the main characteristic of concentrated organic manures?

options.a: They have lower nutrient content than bulky manures.
options.b: They are required in large quantities in the field.
options.c: They have higher nutrient content and are used in smaller quantities.

questions.explanation: Concentrated organic manures have a higher nutrient content than bulky organic manures and are applied in smaller amounts.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Why are concentrated organic manures also called organic nitrogen fertilizers?

options.b: They provide nitrogen directly in an inorganic form.
options.c: Their organic nitrogen is converted into ammoniacal and nitrate nitrogen by bacterial action.

questions.explanation: Before crops can use the nitrogen in concentrated organic manures, it must be broken down by bacteria into ammoniacal and nitrate nitrogen.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a concentrated organic manure?
questions.explanation: Oil cakes, blood meal, and fish meal are examples of concentrated organic manures due to their high nutrient content.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an edible oilcake?
questions.explanation: Edible oilcakes- are those which can be safely fed to the livestock ex groundnut cake, coconut cake, etc. Non edible oilcakes- which are not fit for feeding livestock ex-castor cake, neem cake, mahua cake.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following non-edible oilcakes has the highest nitrogen content?
questions.explanation: Safflower cake contains 4.9% nitrogen, which is the highest among the listed non-edible oilcakes.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which non-edible oilcake has the highest phosphorus (P2O5) content?
questions.explanation: Castor cake has 1.8% phosphorus (P2O5), which is the highest among Mahua Cake, Safflower Cake, and Cotton Seed Cake.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which edible oilcake has the highest nitrogen (N) content?
questions.explanation: Groundnut cake has the highest nitrogen (N) content (7.3%) among common edible oilcakes.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which edible oilcake has the highest phosphorus (P2O5) content?
questions.explanation: Cotton seed cake (decorticated) has the highest phosphorus (P2O5) content at 2.8%.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which edible oilcake has the highest potassium (K2O) content?
questions.explanation: Cotton seed cake (decorticated) has the highest potassium (K2O) content at 1.8%.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which organic manure has the highest nitrogen (N) content?
questions.explanation: Blood meal contains 10-12% nitrogen, which is the highest among the listed organic manures.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which organic manure has the highest phosphorus (P2O5) content?
questions.explanation: Fish meal has a phosphorus (P2O5) content ranging from 3-9%, which is the highest among the listed organic manures.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which organic manure has the lowest potassium (K2O) content?
questions.explanation: Meat meal has 0.5% potassium (K2O), which is on the lower end compared to others like blood meal.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is the primary function of soil amendments?

options.a: To increase pest resistance in crops
options.b: To influence plant growth by improving soil conditions
options.c: To act as a direct source of plant nutrients

questions.explanation: Soil amendments improve soil reactions, alter nutrient availability, and enhance physical conditions, thereby promoting plant growth.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a soil amendment that improves soil structure?
questions.explanation: Gypsum helps improve soil structure by reducing soil compaction and enhancing water infiltration, especially in sodic soils.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which soil amendment is commonly used to lower soil pH in alkaline soils?
questions.explanation: Sulfur is used as a soil amendment to reduce soil pH in alkaline soils by increasing acidity.[cite: 5]

questions.question: How are fertilizers classified based on the number of nutrients they supply?
questions.explanation: Straight fertilizers contain only one primary nutrient (e.g., urea - N only). Complex fertilizers contain two or more essential nutrients chemically combined (e.g., DAP-N & P). Mixed fertilizers are physical mixtures of two or more fertilizers (e.g., NPK 10:26:26).[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a straight fertilizer?
questions.explanation: Urea (46% N) contains only nitrogen, making it a straight fertilizer.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which fertilizer is considered a complex fertilizer?
questions.explanation: DAP contains nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P2O5) in a chemically combined form, making it a complex fertilizer.[cite: 5]

questions.question: How are fertilizers classified as low analysis or high analysis?

options.a: Based on the price of the fertilizer
options.b: Based on the solubility of nutrients in water
options.c: Based on the total percentage of primary nutrients
options.d: Based on whether they are organic or inorganic

questions.explanation: They are classified based on the total percentage of primary nutrients they contain.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is the primary difference between low-analysis and high-analysis fertilizers?

options.a: Low-analysis fertilizers contain more than 25% nutrients
options.b: High-analysis fertilizers contain less than 25% nutrients
options.c: Low-analysis fertilizers contain less than 25% nutrients, while high-analysis fertilizers contain more than 25% nutrients
options.d: Low-analysis fertilizers are always organic, while high-analysis fertilizers are inorganic

questions.explanation: Low-analysis fertilizers contain less than 25% total primary nutrients (N, P2O5, K2O). High-analysis fertilizers contain more than 25% total primary nutrients.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a low-analysis fertilizer?
questions.explanation: SSP contains only 16% P2O5 making it a low-analysis fertilizer.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which fertilizer is classified as a high-analysis fertilizer?
questions.explanation: Urea contains 46% nitrogen (N), making it a high-analysis fertilizer.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which fertilizer contains the highest percentage of nitrogen (N)?
questions.explanation: Anhydrous Ammonia contains 82.2% nitrogen (N), which is the highest among the given fertilizers. Urea contains 46% N, which is lower than anhydrous ammonia. DAP and Ammonium Phosphates have lower nitrogen content.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Diammonium Phosphate (DAP) contains how much phosphorus (P2O5)?
questions.explanation: DAP (Diammonium Phosphate) contains 18% nitrogen (N) and 46% phosphorus (P2O5). It is a widely used high-analysis fertilizer that provides both nitrogen and phosphorus for plant growth.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which fertilizer provides both nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P2O5) in equal amounts?
questions.explanation: Ammonium Phosphates contain 20% nitrogen (N) and 20% phosphorus (P2O5), making the ratio 1:1.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of nitrate fertilizers?

options.b: Highly soluble and prone to leaching

questions.explanation: Nitrate fertilizers increase soil alkalinity as their residual effect is basic in nature. They are highly mobile and soluble, making them prone to leaching. They are used as top dressing due to their quick availability to plants. In waterlogged conditions, they undergo denitrification, leading to nitrogen loss.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a nitrate fertilizer?
questions.explanation: Calcium nitrate (Ca(NO3)2) and Sodium nitrate (NaNO3) are nitrate fertilizers. Urea and Ammonium sulfate contain nitrogen in ammonium form (NH4+), not nitrate (NO3-). DAP and Superphosphate primarily supply phosphorus, not nitrate nitrogen.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an ammoniacal fertilizer?
questions.explanation: Ammoniacal fertilizers contain nitrogen in the form of ammonium (NH4+). Ammonium sulfate (NH4)2SO4 is a well-known ammoniacal fertilizer, containing about 20% nitrogen.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of ammoniacal fertilizers?

options.d: Contains the lowest nitrogen percentage among fertilizers

questions.explanation: Ammoniacal fertilisers- Fertiliser contains nitrogen in the form of ammonium. Characteristics - Radially soluble hence easily available to plants. Adsorb on clay complex hence fewer leaching losses. Well suited for submerged soils.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following ammoniacal fertilizers contains the highest percentage of nitrogen?
questions.explanation: Anhydrous ammonium contains highest amount of Nitrogen among any fertiliser that is 82%.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an amide fertilizer?
questions.explanation: Amide fertilizers contain nitrogen in the form of amide (-CONH2), making them organic fertilizers. Urea (CO(NH2)2) is an amide fertilizer containing 46%.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following fertilizers contains nitrogen in both nitrate and ammonium forms?
questions.explanation: Nitrate and ammoniacal fertilizers contain nitrogen in both nitrate (NO3-) and ammonium (NH4+) forms, ensuring quick and sustained nitrogen release. Ammonium nitrate (NH4NO3) has both NH4+ (ammonium) and NO3- (nitrate), making it a perfect example of this category.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding slow-release nitrogenous fertilizers?

options.a: They release nitrogen quickly and are prone to leaching.
options.b: Urea is the most effective slow-release nitrogen fertilizer without any modification.
options.c: Slow-release fertilizers reduce the frequency of nitrogen application but may have limited availability in early growth stages.
options.d: They have the highest availability in the first few days of application.

questions.explanation: Slow-release fertilizers provide nitrogen gradually, reducing the need for frequent applications and minimizing losses. They may have limited nitrogen availability in the early growth stages because the nutrients take time to become plant-available.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which nitrogen fertilizer is most prone to volatilization if left on the soil surface?
questions.explanation: Urea hydrolyzes to ammonium, increasing pH near the soil surface, which promotes ammonia gas loss.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is the primary form of nitrogen lost during volatilization?
questions.explanation: Ammonia (NH3) is the gaseous form lost due to volatilization.[cite: 5]

questions.question: In which type of soil is nitrogen leaching most severe?

options.a: Clay soil with high cation exchange capacity
options.c: Sandy soil with low organic matter

questions.explanation: Sandy soils drain quickly and have low nutrient-holding capacity, leading to high leaching.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following phosphatic fertilizers is water-soluble?
questions.explanation: Water-soluble phosphatic fertilizers readily dissolve in water, making phosphorus immediately available to plants. SSP (Single Superphosphate) contains water-soluble P2O5.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which phosphatic fertilizer belongs to the "citric acid-soluble" category?
questions.explanation: Citric acid-soluble fertilizers are not fully water-soluble but dissolve in weak acids, making phosphorus slowly available to plants. Dicalcium phosphate (CaHPO4) falls into this category.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which phosphatic fertilizer is the least available to crops due to poor solubility?
questions.explanation: Phosphoric acid not soluble in water or citric acid is the least available to plants. Basic slag, containing tricalcium phosphate, is an example of a poorly soluble phosphatic fertilizer.[cite: 5]

questions.question: How does soil pH affect phosphatic fertilizer efficiency?

options.a: Phosphorus availability is highest in strongly acidic soils (pH < 5.5)
options.c: Neutral to slightly acidic soils (pH 6-7) provide optimal phosphorus availability
options.d: Phosphorus does not react with soil pH

questions.explanation: Phosphorus availability is highest in neutral to slightly acidic soils (pH 6-7).[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following phosphatic fertilizers has the highest phosphorus content?
questions.explanation: Monoammonium phosphate (MAP) contains 48% P2O5, the highest.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which phosphatic fertilizer provides both nitrogen and phosphorus in equal amounts?
questions.explanation: Ammonium phosphate contains 20% phosphorus and 20% nitrogen, making it a balanced N-P fertilizer.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following fertilizers is most suitable for acidic soils due to its sulfur content?
questions.explanation: APS contains sulfur (from sulfate), which helps neutralize soil alkalinity and is beneficial for sulfur-deficient soils.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which phosphatic fertilizer is most commonly used for direct soil application due to its high solubility?
questions.explanation: TSP (46-48% P2O5) is highly water-soluble and widely used for direct application.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which fertilizer provides the highest phosphorus efficiency for crops with high phosphorus demand?
questions.explanation: MAP (48% P2O5) provides the highest phosphorus content and has good solubility, making it ideal for phosphorus-demanding crops.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following phosphatic fertilizers is primarily citric acid-soluble?
questions.explanation: Dicalcium phosphate (CaHPO4) is citric acid-soluble, meaning it is not immediately available but dissolves in weak acids over time.[cite: 5]

questions.question: In which type of soil are citric acid-soluble phosphatic fertilizers most effective?
questions.explanation: Citric acid-soluble fertilizers release phosphorus efficiently in neutral soils where weak acids from roots enhance solubility.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following is a major disadvantage of citric acid-soluble phosphatic fertilizers?

options.b: They are highly water-soluble and prone to leaching
options.c: Their phosphorus availability depends on soil acidity and microbial activity
options.d: They contain high levels of nitrogen

questions.explanation: Citric acid-soluble fertilizers depend on soil acidity and microbial action to break down phosphorus into an available form, making their efficiency variable.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which citric acid-soluble phosphatic fertilizer is commonly used as an animal feed supplement?
questions.explanation: Dicalcium phosphate (DCP) is not only a fertilizer but also used in animal feed due to its moderate solubility and bioavailability.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following potassic fertilizers is NOT suitable for sugarcane cultivation?
questions.explanation: MOP (Potassium chloride) is not suitable for sugarcane because chloride ions reduce sugar accumulation.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Why is potassium chloride (MOP) not recommended for tobacco crops?

options.b: It reduces burning quality of the leaf

questions.explanation: MOP reduces the burning quality of tobacco leaves, making them less desirable for commercial use.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which non-chloride potassic fertilizer contains both nitrogen and potassium?
questions.explanation: Potassium nitrate (KNO3), also called saltpeter, contains 13% nitrogen and 44% K2O, making it a dual-purpose fertilizer.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which potassic fertilizer is best suited for fruit trees and vegetables?
questions.explanation: Potassium nitrate is an excellent fertilizer for fruit trees and vegetables because it provides both potassium and nitrogen without chloride toxicity.[cite: 5]

questions.question: At which growth stages should fertilizers be applied in wheat for maximum nutrient efficiency?

options.c: Basal, crown root initiation, and panicle initiation

questions.explanation: Wheat requires fertilizer application at three key stages: Basal (before sowing) for early growth, Crown root initiation (CRI) to support root development, and Panicle initiation for better grain formation.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which of the following crops typically requires fertilizer application at 60, 90, and 120 days after planting?
questions.explanation: Sugarcane is a long-duration crop that requires multiple split applications at 60, 90, and 120 days after planting to sustain its high nutrient demand.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Why is basal fertilizer application essential for pulses and groundnut?

options.b: To increase nitrogen fixation in soil directly
options.c: To improve flowering and pod formation

questions.explanation: Leguminous crops like pulses and groundnut rely on early nutrient availability to develop strong roots and nodules for nitrogen fixation.[cite: 5]

questions.question: Which cereal crop requires fertilizer application at both basal and panicle initiation but NOT at tillering?
questions.explanation: Sorghum requires fertilizer application at basal and panicle initiation stages but does not need an additional dose at tillering.[cite: 5]

questions.question: What is the main reason for applying fertilizers at the panicle initiation stage in cereal crops?

options.b: To support grain filling and increase yield

questions.explanation: Panicle initiation is a crucial stage where plants transition from vegetative to reproductive growth. Applying fertilizer at this stage enhances grain filling and final yield.[cite: 5]
